chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know any Hajj for God other than Al-Mut'ah. When we meet our Lord, we say: O our Lord, we acted according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet. And the people say: We acted according to our own opinion. So God will place us and them wherever He wills.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Al-Mut'ah (a specific type of pilgrimage, often associated with Umrah al-Mut'ah or the combined Hajj and Umrah in Shia fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Al-Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that 'Hajj al-Mut'ah' (combining Umrah and Hajj without separation) is the only form of Hajj authentically known to the Ahl al-Bayt, contrasting it with the 'ra'y' (personal opinion) of the general populace. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering strictly to the Quran and Prophetic Sunnah rather than juristic innovation, with the final verdict left to God. The narration serves as a theological basis for the Shia practice of performing Umrah and Hajj as a single, continuous ritual.
